title: Unobservables and Decoherence from Complexity
summary: The interface between the quantum and the classical is an intriguing and, at times, hotly contested subject of ongoing research. The quantum regime is characterized by interference, made possible by the superposition principle, while such phenomena are absent in macroscopic, everyday experience. Here, we investigate the link of this absence (or, as we will argue, unobservability) to computational complexity.
